hook.line: The last thing a talk or an essay says is the thing people remember. In Spanish the ending has its own set phrases, and they are easy to borrow.
hook.es: Para terminar, les dejo una pregunta.
hook.en: To finish, I'll leave you with a question. (to an audience)

examples.es: En resumen, cocinar no es difícil.
Para terminar, les dejo una pregunta.
examples.en: To finish, I'll leave you with a question. (to an audience)

examples.es: En conclusión, todos podemos hacer algo.
examples.en: In conclusion, we can all do something.
Thank you very much for your attention.

examples.es: Para concluir, el café es de todos.
examples.en: To conclude, the café belongs to everyone.

rule:
Close with one of these, then a comma and the summary:

*Para terminar,*
*En resumen,*
*En conclusión,*

Nothing new goes in the conclusion. Say again, in a sentence, what you have already said.

Then close the talk itself: *Bueno, eso es todo. Muchas gracias por su atención.* The phrase *su atención* is formal, which is right for an audience.
smallPrint: Teachers call these closing markers, or *marcadores de cierre*.

readAndPick.es: En resumen, cocinar no es difícil.
options: In short, cooking isn't difficult.
First, cooking isn't difficult.
What's more, cooking isn't difficult.

readAndPick.es: Para terminar, les dejo una pregunta.
options: To start, I'll ask you a question. (to an audience)
To finish, I'll leave you with a question. (to an audience)
To finish, he leaves you with a question.

readAndPick.es: En conclusión, todos podemos hacer algo.
options: In conclusion, we can all do something.
Firstly, we can all do something.
In conclusion, I can do something.
Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you very much for your attention.
Thank you very much for your time.
Well, that's all.
Well, that's good.
Well, that's everything I know.

readAndPick.es: Para concluir, el café es de todos.
options: To begin, the café belongs to everyone.
Besides, the café belongs to everyone.
To conclude, the café belongs to everyone.
To conclude, we need more time.
Lastly, we need more time.
Firstly, we need more time.
In short, we're not selling.
At first, we're not selling.
On the other hand, we're not selling.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right opener and type the whole sentence (In short, we're not selling): *___, no vendemos.* (*En resumen* or *Además*)
Type in Spanish (to an audience): To finish, I'll leave you with a question.
yourTurn.answer: Para terminar, les dejo una pregunta.
accept: Para terminar les dejo una pregunta.
yourTurn.why: *Para terminar* closes, and *les* is the audience.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In conclusion, we can all do something.
yourTurn.answer: En conclusión, todos podemos hacer algo.
accept: En conclusión todos podemos hacer algo.
yourTurn.why: *En conclusión* leads into the last idea, and *todos* means "all of us".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In short, cooking isn't difficult.
yourTurn.answer: En resumen, cocinar no es difícil.
accept: En resumen, cocinar no es tan difícil.
yourTurn.why: *Cocinar* is an infinitive used as the subject.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Thank you very much for your attention.
yourTurn.why: *Su atención* is the formal way to thank a group.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Well, that's all.
yourTurn.why: *Eso es todo* tells people you have finished.

yourTurn.prompt: Change the opener so it means "To conclude": *Para terminar, el café es de todos.*
yourTurn.answer: Para concluir, el café es de todos.
accept: En conclusión, el café es de todos.
yourTurn.why: *Para concluir* and *para terminar* are the same idea.

pitfalls.wrong: En corto, el café es de todos.
pitfalls.right: En resumen, el café es de todos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "In short" is not *en corto*; Spanish says *en resumen*.
To an audience, use the formal *su*, not *tu*.

pitfalls.wrong: En resumen, además, el café es de todos.
pitfalls.right: En resumen, el café es de todos.
pitfalls.why: A closing line adds nothing new, so *además* has no place there.

personal: Close a tiny talk about your week: *Para terminar,* or *En resumen,* followed by one sentence, then *Muchas gracias por su atención*.
